card.summary: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies federal housing programs and banking regulations to address housing supply, affordability, and regulatory hurdles. It creates pilot programs and grant initiatives for housing repairs, conversions of empty buildings, small-dollar mortgages, and manufactured housing without permanent chassis. It also adjusts environmental review rules under NEPA, alters bank investment limits, modifies the HOME Investment Partnerships program, and restricts the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency.

summary: The Housing Supply Expansion Act of 2025 updates federal law to include homes built without a permanent chassis in the definition of a manufactured home. It directs the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to issue revised safety and construction standards for these homes and requires states to certify that their laws treat manufactured homes without a permanent chassis the same as those with a permanent chassis regarding financing, taxes, and other areas.

affected_groups.effect: May produce manufactured homes without a permanent chassis, subject to new federal standards, labels, data plates, and invoice notations.

Must submit initial certifications and annual recertifications to the Secretary regarding the regulatory parity of manufactured homes, or face prohibitions on manufacturing, installation, or sale of certain homes.

May purchase manufactured homes built without a permanent chassis that are regulated and treated similarly to traditional manufactured homes in financing, titling, insurance, and taxes, provided their state complies with certification rules.

key_provisions: Updates the definition of a manufactured home in the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974 to allow homes built with or without a permanent chassis.

Requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to issue revised standards for manufactured homes built without a permanent chassis, including distinct labels, data plates, and invoice notations.

Requires states to submit an initial certification within one year (or two years for biennially meeting legislatures) confirming that state laws treat manufactured homes without a permanent chassis in parity with traditional manufactured homes.
Requires states to submit annual recertifications confirming that new state laws do not change the parity of manufactured home regulations.
Prohibits the manufacture, installation, or sale of covered manufactured homes without a permanent chassis in states that fail to submit the required certifications on time.
Authorizes the Secretary to coordinate with other federal agencies to ensure consistent treatment of manufactured homes across federal laws and regulations.
missing_information: Specific details on what safety and construction standards will be written for homes without a permanent chassis.
Exact funding amounts or administrative costs associated with updating standards, providing model guidance, and tracking state certifications.

summary_detail.significance: This bill makes a moderate change to federal housing standards by officially recognizing manufactured homes built without a permanent chassis and tying their continued production, sale, and installation to state-level regulatory compliance.
